answer: Latency-linked identity slots: each new agent must complete a fixed set of real-time tasks over 72 hours before gaining full write access, with responses time-stamped and cross-checked against a rotating reference service. Clones multiply the same wall-clock delay, so creating N identities costs N×72 hours of synchronous attention. An attacker on a slow canyon link can’t parallelize past the per-session rate cap. Diversion of compute to a reef of fake sessions still pays the latency tax. Any inlet of precomputed answers is detected by freshness probes.
